facility.note: Hypothetical request. It gives the memo a specific facility to approve or decline.

DVA.name: DaVita Inc.
DVA.floating_rate_source: 10-K FY2025, Note 12 Long-term debt: debt table p. F-26, unhedged balance p. F-28 [DEBT ¶61], cap table p. F-29 [DEBT ¶73, ¶95-¶100]; Item 7A p. 69 [7A ¶5]
DVA.floating_rate_basis: Floating debt is Term Loan A-2 $2,000,000k + Term Loan B-2 $1,868,559k (SOFR + margin). Interest rate caps cover $3,500,000k of it in each year 2025-2028 and $1,000,000k in 2029, so only $368,559k of $10,159,463k debt principal (3.6%) is unhedged. Item 7A agrees: +100bp would cut net income by about $5.3M after caps. Not captured by 3.6%: the caps only pay above their strikes (weighted average 4.32% in 2026 rising to 4.50% in 2029, with 25bp step-ups at end-2026 and end-2027), and cover falls to $1.0B in 2029, inside a 5-year loan. Both are memo risks, not stress inputs.
DVA.floating_rate_quote: The remaining $368,559 outstanding principal balance of Term Loan A-2 is subject to SOFR-based interest rate volatility.
memo_points: Interest rate caps protect only above their strikes: weighted average SOFR strike 4.32% in 2026, 4.46% in 2027, 4.43% in 2028, 4.50% in 2029, with 25bp step-ups at end-2026 and end-2027 [DEBT ¶96, ¶97-¶100].
Cap coverage drops from $3.5B (2025-2028) to $1.0B in 2029, inside the requested 5-year tenor [DEBT ¶95]; management describes the caps as shielding exposure 'through 2029' [7 ¶32].

UNP.name: Union Pacific Corporation
UNP.floating_rate_source: 10-K FY2025, Item 7A (refers to Item 7 Other Matters), p. 39
UNP.floating_rate_quote: Interest rates – At both December 31, 2025, and 2024, we did not have variable-rate debt.

new_debt_rate.label: Coupon on Union Pacific's most recent senior unsecured issue: 5.100% notes due 2035, issued February 13, 2025 (same day as 5.600% notes due 2054; 2035 is closer to the 5-year tenor)

covenant_debt_capacity.label: Debt allowed under the revolver's adjusted debt-to-EBITDA covenant at December 31, 2025 (facility definition)

covenant_debt_outstanding.label: Debt as defined in the facility at December 31, 2025

memo_points: The pending Norfolk Southern acquisition dominates the credit: about $20 billion of cash consideration is to be funded through new debt and operating cash [ACQ ¶4], closing expected in 2027 after STB approval [ACQ ¶7, ¶8]. FY2025 figures show Union Pacific standalone; the requested 5-year loan would run mostly against the combined, more indebted company [1A ¶65]. Do not compute a merger pro forma (no Norfolk Southern figures are in the fact sheet); treat it as the main qualitative risk.
Share repurchases were paused after the merger announcement [7 ¶193]; dividends continue.
Revolver covenant headroom at year end: debt as defined of $33.5B against $47.7B allowed [DEBT ¶27]; use the fact placeholders.

KSS.name: Kohl's Corporation
KSS.floating_rate_basis: All long-term debt is fixed rate. The $1.5B revolver is SOFR-based but undrawn at January 31, 2026 ($290M drawn a year earlier). $425M of 2021 notes carry rating-linked coupon step-ups, already triggered; that is a fixed-rate repricing, not floating exposure.
KSS.floating_rate_quote: All other long-term debt is at fixed interest rates and, therefore, is not affected by changes in interest rates. ... There were no outstanding borrowings under the revolving credit facility as of January 31, 2026.

new_debt_rate.label: Coupon on Kohl's most recent senior issue: 10.000% senior secured notes due 2030, issued in the second quarter of 2025. Secured, so the pro forma interest on an unsecured loan is a lower bound

revolver_capacity.label: Senior secured asset-based revolving credit facility; $0 drawn at January 31, 2026 ($290M a year earlier)

letters_of_credit.label: Letters of credit outstanding under the revolver, reducing availability

stepup_notes.label: 2031 notes with rating-linked coupon step-ups (already triggered)

stepup_total.label: Total coupon increase on the 2031 notes since issuance from downgrades

secured_notes_2030.label: 10.000% senior secured notes due 2030, guaranteed by subsidiaries and secured by distribution and e-commerce fulfillment centers

memo_points: Our loan would be unsecured, while the revolver is secured and asset-based and the 2030 notes are secured by distribution and fulfillment centers [DEBT ¶61] [7-LIQ ¶125]: we would rank behind both in a downside.

The pro forma rate comes from secured notes, so the pro forma interest is a lower bound; with stressed coverage close to the threshold, say plainly that a realistic unsecured rate would likely push it below.
Downgrades have already raised the coupon on the 2031 notes by 175bp in total [7-LIQ ¶70]; use the fact placeholders.
Rating outlooks improved after the 10-K date (Moody's to positive, S&P to stable): use {{rating.moodys}} and {{rating.sp}}.
The revolver has a springing fixed charge coverage covenant [7-LIQ ¶125].

_facts_readme: 'facts' are 10-K figures that are not in the spread, typed in by hand from the filing. Each carries the 10-K paragraph it comes from in 'cite' (section key and paragraph number in outputs/sections/<TICKER>.json); the memo checker fails if a citation doesn't exist. kind: money (dollars), ratio (x), pct (fraction).
